title: fix(plugin-auth,platform-objects): revoke a session by its row id, resolved server-side
body:
Security fix (maintainer-ordered; no public card; detail withheld under the disclosure ruling).

Clause-②: no

## The invariant

Setup → Diagnostics → Sessions (and Account → Active Sessions): a row's **Revoke Session** ends the session it names, and that session's next request is refused. It works for the session's owner and for a platform administrator, and for nobody else. No request to or answer from the revoke path carries a session token, and `sys_session.token` stays `internal: true`.

## What changed

- **`packages/platform-objects`**: `sys_session` `revoke_session` is keyed on the row's `id`, which every list row carries. It sets `recordIdParam: 'sessionId'`, and `recordIdField` falls back to its default `id`. It posts to `POST /api/v1/auth/sys-session/revoke`. The `token` field is unchanged: `internal`, `hidden`, `readonly`. The console runtime is generic, so objectui needs no change.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-auth`**: new ObjectStack mount `POST /api/v1/auth/sys-session/revoke`. The handler is `sys-session-revoke.ts`, the mount is in `auth-plugin.ts`, and the route is in `auth-route-ledger.ts` plus its conformance pin. The server looks up the session from the id through better-auth's own storage adapter, which hides ended sessions and re-attaches the internal column server-side. The token is used only inside the server.
  - **The owner lane** forwards the request in-process to better-auth's `POST /revoke-session`, with the caller's own credentials. That route's ownership and freshness checks still apply, and so do the existing admission guard and the `user_revoked` tombstone, all unchanged.
  - **The administrator lane** handles another user's session. The ADR-0068 D2 `judgePlatformAdmin` admits the caller (held sessions are refused per ADR-0069 D3). The session is then tombstoned in place with `revoke_reason: admin` (ADR-0069 D4). This is the same row shape `membership-ended-session.ts` and `forced-reset-revocation.ts` write. The reason value comes from the interactive-revoke ledger, so the two cannot drift. better-auth's `/admin/revoke-user-session` is not used as the delegate: it authorizes on the legacy `role` scalar, which ADR-0068 D2 administrators do not carry.
  - **Every other signed-in caller** gets one `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, byte-identical to the answer for an id that names no live session. An anonymous caller gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, and a body without `sessionId` gets `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.
  - The route is not under `/api/v1/auth/admin/`, because its first lane admits the owner. It belongs to the `sys-oauth-application/register` family.
- **`session-tombstone.ts`**: one comment sentence. The `admin` reason now has a third writer.
- **Tenant-audit census**: `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` were regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, and the page's hand-written figures were moved from 231 to 232. The administrator lane's tombstone write is a new engine write call site, and `check-tenant-audit-census` requires it to be counted.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/sys-session-revoke-by-id.md`, a patch for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`.

## Tests

All on this branch. `plugin-auth` resolves the subject through relative source imports, so its runs read `src/`.

- **New pins**, in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sys-session-revoke.test.ts`. They run through the plugin's real route registration on a real Hono app, in front of a real `AuthManager`, with cookies minted by better-auth's own sign-in. Every revoke asserts both halves: the cookie stops authenticating, and the row survives with its cause. Every refusal asserts that the target still authenticates and its row is untouched, as `status` plus `code`.
  - an administrator revoking another user's session by id ends it, so that session's next request is refused (`revoke_reason: admin`, and the administrator's own session is untouched);
  - a session's owner revoking their own other session by id ends that one and keeps the current one (`user_revoked`);
  - an already-ended session reads not-found, and its record keeps the first ending;
  - a signed-in caller without platform-admin standing cannot revoke another user's session (`404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, byte-identical to an id that names nothing);
  - an anonymous caller is refused before anything is revoked (`401 UNAUTHENTICATED`);
  - a request that names no session is refused, and nothing is revoked (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`);
  - the administrator lane records the interactive-revoke ledger's own `admin` value.
  - Each answer above is also asserted to carry no session token.
- **New pins**, in `packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts`:
  - `revoke_session` identifies its session by the row id and posts `sessionId` to the new route;
  - `sys_session.token` stays `internal`, `hidden` and `readonly`;
  - no identity action identifies its record by a field the server never serves. This sweep covers every identity object and has a positive control.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` reported Test Files 166 passed (166) and Tests 3185 passed, 10 skipped (3195).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` passed: src, examples and the test layer (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test` reported Test Files 79 passed (79) and Tests 1198 passed (1198). `typecheck` passed.
- **After merging `origin/main`** (74f78159a): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `@objectstack/spec` build, then `check:generated` ("All 14 generated artifacts are up to date"), then `plugin-auth` and `platform-objects` typecheck. All passed.
- **Ablations.** Each one mutated one line, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed). Each restore was proven: blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The direction was predicted before each run, and every result matched the prediction.
  - A1, the standing check removed from the administrator lane: 1 red, the non-admin pin.
  - A2, the administrator tombstone write removed: 2 red, the admin pin and the already-ended pin.
  - A3, the owner lane removed: 1 red, the owner pin.
  - A4, the action re-keyed to `token`: 2 red, the declaration pin and the sweep.

  - `check:i18n`, reason: it needs the built CLI closure. No translatable string changed: the action's label, confirm text and success message are byte-identical.
